name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply formatting-only patches to third-party dependencies.

This keeps our codebase clean without risking logic changes. The trade-off is we won’t catch deeper issues in dependencies, but that’s better handled by dedicated security tools. It’s safe, fast, and directly improves readability.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just "skipping deeper logic fixes"—it’s that formatting-only patches mask dependency rot by treating symptoms, not causes. A better alternative: auto-apply *only* when tests pass, then log the diff for human review. Settle it by running a pilot on one dependency and measuring how often tests catch hidden issues.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk is conflating "formatting-only" with "safe"—a formatting patch could still break a dependency if it relies on undocumented whitespace or alignment rules. A better alternative: auto-apply only to dependencies with explicit version pinning and 100% passing tests, then require a human sign-off for any diff larger than 5 lines. Settle it by running a pilot on a single, well-tested dependency and measuring how often the diff triggers a manual review.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Auto-apply formatting-only patches to our own generated code and third-party dependencies with explicit version pinning and 100% passing tests, then log the diff for human review. 
The result must deliver a codebase with improved readability and reduced technical debt, and the lead owns the artifact, a fully implemented and tested auto-apply formatting patch system.
